question: Imagine you are an ENT specialist evaluating a new patient presenting with persistent sore throat, difficulty swallowing, and recent voice changes. evidence: The initial diagnostic approach begins with a thorough medical history.
The initial diagnostic approach includes a physical exam focusing on the oropharynx.
The exam focuses on the tonsils, base of tongue, and lateral/posterior pharyngeal walls.
Risk factors assessed include tobacco and alcohol use.
Risk factors assessed include possible HPV exposure.
Endoscopic evaluation (nasolaryngoscopy or panendoscopy) is performed to visualize the tumor.
A biopsy of the suspicious lesion is essential for histopathological confirmation.
Endoscopic biopsy or fine-needle aspiration (FNA) is used if lymphadenopathy is present.
Biomarker testing for p16 (HPV) status is recommended for all oropharyngeal cancers.
Imaging with contrast-enhanced CT scan or MRI of the neck is critical for accurate staging.
PET/CT is used to evaluate local extension and distant metastasis.

ground_truth: As an ENT specialist, my initial diagnostic approach would begin with a thorough medical history and physical exam, focusing on the oropharynx, tonsils, base of tongue, and lateral/posterior pharyngeal walls. I would assess for risk factors including tobacco, alcohol use, and possible HPV exposure. Next, I would perform endoscopic evaluation (nasolaryngoscopy or panendoscopy) to visualize the tumor and adjacent sites. Biopsy of the suspicious lesion is essential for histopathological confirmation, utilizing endoscopic biopsy or, if lymphadenopathy is present, fine-needle aspiration (FNA) or core needle biopsy (CNB). Biomarker testing for p16 (HPV) status is recommended for all oropharyngeal cancers, as p16 overexpression serves as a surrogate for HPV-mediated disease. Imaging with contrast-enhanced CT scan or MRI of the neck, and PET/CT to evaluate both local extension and distant metastasis (lungs, liver, spine), is critical for accurate staging. Dental health assessment and panoramic dental x-ray (Panorex) should be completed prior to treatment. Staging will use the AJCC TNM system, integrating tumor size, nodal involvement, and distant metastasis.
